about: A story as a small graph: claims, each with its label, who said it, when, and the rows and data fields that support it. The page is generated from this file by tools/stories-build.mjs; nothing here is new reporting. See stories/grammar.md for the grammar.
title: The mainland: warned against observed
standfirst: IPMA's warned windows on the mainland opened at 09:00 on Wednesday. This sets what IPMA warned for Lisbon and the other districts beside what has been measured and what has been reported on the ground, as far as the data room holds it.

warnings_in_force.about: The official warnings a weather story states first: IPMA's red warnings for the mainland's districts other than Lisbon (Lisbon's are in sentence n1), resolved from the data room when the page is built and read again in the reader's browser. Never a level of our own.
warnings_in_force.title: IPMA's red warnings for the other mainland districts

sections.title: What has been reported on the ground

claims.text: Red rain warnings stood in eight districts of the mainland on Wednesday morning: Lisboa, Setúbal, Beja and Faro from 09:00 to 18:00 (sent on Tuesday at 21:23), Castelo Branco, Leiria, Santarém and Portalegre from 12:00 to 18:00 (sent at 16:30). IPMA cut them at midday. At 12:18:03 it lowered Castelo Branco, Leiria, Portalegre and Beja to orange, 12:19 to 18:00, and kept Faro red, 12:19 to 18:00. At 12:33:13 it cut Lisboa's and Setúbal's red rain to end at 15:00 (Lisbon then yellow to 18:00). Santarém had no new message. Lisboa's and Setúbal's red rain ended at 15:00 as set. At 15:05:38 IPMA lowered Santarém from red to yellow (and Leiria from orange to yellow), 15:06 to 18:00, as read by the conductor from IPMA's messages and its warnings page at 15:24; the data room's copy of the messages did not hold those two at the 15:23:13 read. At 15:55:03 IPMA lowered Faro's red rain to yellow and its red wind to orange, both 15:56 to 18:00 (row s-1111T1609, its messages as seen in MeteoAlarm's feed at 16:09): no red warning remains on the mainland.
claims.label: fact

claims.text: The wind was warned down twice on Wednesday. At 07:16:30 IPMA lowered Lisboa, Setúbal and Beja from red to orange, 09:00 to 21:00 (Lisbon: "Rajadas até 120 km/h"), and Leiria, Santarém, Portalegre and Évora from red to yellow. At 12:33:13 it cut Lisboa's, Setúbal's and Beja's orange to end at 18:00, Lisbon's now "Rajadas até 90 km/h, podendo atingir 110 km/h nos locais mais expostos". At 15:55:03 it ended the orange wind in Lisboa, Setúbal and Beja and the yellow in Santarém, Évora, Portalegre, Castelo Branco and Leiria at 15:56, and lowered Faro's red wind, 09:00 to 21:00, to orange to 18:00 (row s-1111T1609; the message PO-01-1944 in the data room's copy from the 16:22:55 read; Faro's red message left the feed at 16:09:31): no red wind warning remains on the mainland.
claims.label: fact

claims.text: The sea: an orange warning for the Lisbon coast from 12:00 to 21:00, "Ondas de sudoeste com 5 a 7 metros e que poderão atingir até 13 metros de altura máxima", sent on Tuesday at 12:09.
claims.label: fact

supports.expect: Ondas de sudoeste com 5 a 7 metros e que poderão atingir até 13 metros de altura máxima.

claims.text: Inside the windows so far (they opened at 09:00 on Wednesday), the airport's fifteen reports from 09:00 to 16:00 fall in two parts. Until 13:30 the wind was 17 to 28 km/h, backing from south-south-east through east to east-north-east and then east again, with no gust reported, heavy rain from 10:30 and visibility down to 1.5 km at 13:00. Between 13:30 and 14:00 the wind turned from east to south and rose from 17 to 54 km/h, gusting 74 km/h (40 knots), with wind shear reported on runway 20 and the temperature up 2 °C; at 15:00 it was south-south-west 41 km/h gusting 61 km/h, the rain over and visibility above 10 km, wind shear still reported; at 15:30 and 16:00 south-south-west 37 and 39 km/h (gusting 61 at 15:30, no gust at 16:00), light rain and drizzle again and visibility 1.5 km. The pressure fell from 1001 to 989 hPa by 14:00 and held at 989 to 16:00. IPMA's newest station hour is the one labelled 15:00: the rain all but stopped (0.0 to 1.2 mm at seven stations, Relógio the most) and the mean wind eased to 17.6 to 36.7 km/h, all from the south-west, Relógio the strongest; before it, the hour labelled 14:00 had 1.2 to 6.8 mm and up to 41.0 km/h at Oeiras, the strongest mean wind of the day, and the hour labelled 13:00 5.9 to 26.2 mm (Oeiras, the heaviest single hour at IPMA's Lisbon stations in the data room's record of the storm). The 74 km/h gust is below the gust warned for its hour (90 km/h, 110 in the most exposed places). The red rain ended at 15:00 as set. At 15:55:03 IPMA ended the orange wind at 15:56, two hours early (its message, in the data room's copy from the 16:22:55 read). So the wind window is over: in the airport's reports inside it, from 09:00 to 15:30, no gust reached the warned gust, the strongest 74 km/h at 14:00. Yellow rain stands to 18:00, the orange sea to 21:00.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA's stations and the airport's METAR, as read

claims.text: The strongest gust in the airport's reports we hold is now 40 knots (74 km/h), from the south at 14:00 on Wednesday, inside the window; before it, the strongest was 36 knots (67 km/h), on Tuesday at 11:00. The gust warned for that hour is 90 km/h, 110 in the most exposed places, and the data room's list of airport gusts above the gust warned for their hour, kept from 05:00 on Wednesday, is still empty.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: the data room's comparison of the airport's reports with the warned gust

supports.note: A tripwire: the data room lists here every airport gust from Wed 05:00 above the gust warned for that hour. Empty at this read.

claims.text: The airport's own forecast for pilots was lowered at 10:08, and the forecast issued at 11:00 repeats the cut: at times between 12:00 and 16:00, 20 knots gusting 35 (65 km/h), with a 30% chance of gusts of 55 knots (102 km/h) in thunderstorms. Amended at 14:36: 70 km/h gusts to 16:00, then west-north-west, at times gusting 50 km/h from 18:00 to 21:00, and no thunderstorm group. It is a point forecast for the airport, not a public warning; IPMA's public warnings above are unchanged by it.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA, the TAF for Lisbon airport (a point forecast for pilots, not a public warning)

claims.text: The counts of occurrences so far come from the press, not from civil protection's own site, and they are not one series. Lusa gave 66 on the mainland at 03:30 as civil protection's figure; CNN Portugal's live blog later gave 60 by 06:00, with Greater Lisbon the most affected at 26; Observador's title, citing civil protection, has 189 on the mainland by 11:00. VOST Portugal, volunteers and not an authority, posted at 13:03 that there were 538 occurrences in Portugal up to 12:00, mainly fallen trees and floods, naming no source. The counts do not cover the same period or come from the same report.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: Lusa (via Notícias ao Minuto) and CNN Portugal's live blog; nothing read at ANEPC

claims.text: Overnight, CNN Portugal's live blog reported four floods in Greater Lisbon and the Setúbal peninsula, and the Porto Brandão–Trafaria–Algés ferry suspended for Wednesday; it later reported intense rain may coincide with high tide and hinder drainage in the big cities.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: CNN Portugal's live blog; nothing read at the ferry operator or ANEPC

claims.text: Beside the venue: nearly ten cars partly submerged at Parque das Nações, by Oriente, on Wednesday morning (CNN Portugal, 07:24, with photos at 09:28), and Lisbon's riverside almost empty with access restricted (09:20).
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: CNN Portugal's live blog; not confirmed at a public body

claims.text: Roads and flights: the Vasco da Gama bridge limited to 100 km/h because of the weather (Lusa, 09:24; the bridges had no restrictions on Tuesday night). 222 flights cancelled by 09:20, 208 at Lisbon and 14 at Faro, according to the airports' operator ANA's site as reported by CNN Portugal at 09:54. Neither was read at the operator itself.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: Lusa; CNN Portugal citing ANA's site

claims.text: So the two sides can only begin to be set against each other. Inside the windows, which opened at 09:00, the airport has reported no gust and a wind of at most 28 km/h against orange gusts warned (up to 120 km/h until 12:33, up to 90 since), while the rain has been heavy, up to 18.7 mm in a station hour under a red rain warning. IPMA itself now writes of less wind than it forecast on Tuesday. Most of what is known on the ground is still the press. This is our comparison, not a finding: it takes the weakest label of what it compares.
claims.label: evidence

claims.text: The government's crisis cabinet line leads the live pages late on Wednesday morning: "O mais complicado ainda vai acontecer" (RTP) and "Governo insiste na prevenção e avisa que tempestade ainda não chegou" (ECO). In the afternoon DN (16:03), Público (16:05) and RTP (16:30) titled the Interior Minister saying «o período mais grave está à porta» («the most serious period is at the door»), said to journalists after the Council of Ministers, by 15:17 at the latest by CNN Portugal's live page: before IPMA's messages of 15:55 ended Lisbon's wind warning and left no red on the mainland. So the minister spoke at least 38 minutes before IPMA's cut, not after it; IPMA decides the warnings. This is the press reporting the government; nothing was read at the government's own pages.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: RTP and ECO, reporting the government

claims.text: Transport at source by late morning: Carris kept its service with priority to essential journeys, interrupted trams 12E, 15E, 18E, 24E, 25E and 28E (15E replaced by buses), closed the Graça funicular from 10:40 and cancelled the Web Summit shuttle lines "devido à suspensão do evento"; its page carries no update time. Fertagus, across the 25 de Abril bridge, ran normally from 05:30, confirmed at 06:30, 08:00, 09:30 and 10:40. The Metro had no service notice on its own site. At 14:40 Transtejo/Soflusa's own notice for the Trafaria – Porto Brandão – Belém crossing said vehicle transport was interrupted for adverse weather and sea, passengers carried only between Porto Brandão and Belém, with no forecast for service to and from Trafaria. CP's own notice (updated 13:30) says, in our words, that it suppressed its Lisbon urban trains between Campolide and Alcântara Terra and four Intercidades over the 25 de Abril bridge in the most critical hours, with no replacement buses, and offers a refund or free exchange on long-distance and regional tickets. VOST Portugal (volunteers, naming no source) also reported rail suspended on the Linha do Norte, the Douro and the Beira Baixa lines. CP's notice updated at 15:30 (changed 16:31) confirms the Beira Baixa: interrupted between Santa Margarida and Tramagal after a landslip; the Linha do Norte and the Douro are still not in it and stay unconfirmed. Fertagus at 16:20: running normally.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: Carris's and Fertagus's own pages, read by incident.researcher@

claims.text: By 11:49 CNN Portugal had 288 flights cancelled in advance at Lisbon airport, the hardest hit (it had 222 at Lisbon and Faro by 09:20). The same page had about 50 weather incidents in Lisbon city overnight, mostly flooding, with no casualties, and Algés seafront closed with the Algés–Trafaria ferry suspended. Not read at ANA, the city or the operator.
claims.label: evidence

claims.text: At 12:32 to 12:35 the press had speed limits on Lisbon's bridges again, 60 km/h on the 25 de Abril and 80 km/h on the Vasco da Gama (Observador, 12:32), and 334 flights cancelled (ECO's live page; CNN Portugal had 288 at 11:49). Nothing was read at Lusoponte's or ANA's own pages.
claims.label: evidence

claims.text: Read at the source: ANA's own figures, situation at 11:00, give Lisbon 565 movements scheduled for Wednesday, 288 cancelled in advance by the airlines, 45 operated and 22 more cancelled by 11:00; Faro 14 of 62 cancelled in advance, Porto 12 of 214, Madeira 20 of 80. Lusoponte's own notice (11:30) limits the 25 de Abril bridge to 60 km/h and the Vasco da Gama to 80 km/h since 11:30, "devido à intensificação da chuva e à visibilidade reduzida", and still advises against wind-prone vehicles crossing. These confirm, at the operators, the press figures in n14 and n15 (334 cancelled, from ECO, is not ANA's figure).
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: ANA's newsroom and Lusoponte's notice, read at source

not_known.text: Civil protection's own count of occurrences on the mainland: none read at ANEPC; the counts above are press reports.
What IPMA's stations measure inside the windows: the station hours from the one labelled 10:00, and the rain total for 09:00 to 18:00, at the next reads.
Whether the flights were cancelled because of the weather, and by whom: the count is the airports' operator's, as reported; no airline's reasons are in the data room.
Observations outside Lisbon (Setúbal, Beja, Faro and the inland districts): the data room holds stations and an airport only for Lisbon and Madeira.
